title: Network evidence playbook: traffic audit + RBAC v2
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working playbook documents a recommended pattern for gathering network-level evidence and audit logs in Redwood private deployments. It ties RBAC v2 decisions, SIEM export mappings, and evidence automation for VPC environments where mTLS and strict firewalling are enforced. The target audience is SREs, platform engineers, and security reviewers preparing customer-ready evidence bundles (SOC/pen test) and SIEM ingestion specs.

Goals:
- Produce reproducible, customer-scoped evidence (network flows, mTLS handshakes, audit events) for compliance requests.
- Define RBAC v2 guardrails so evidence access is auditable and scoped.
- Provide SIEM export schema and automation steps to send sanitized artifacts to customer's SIEM or to our central Security SIEM.
- Document minimal on-host capture and traffic-mirroring runbooks for incident response.

High-level architecture (text diagram):

  customer-vpc (private nodes)            mirror-collector (forensic pod)
  + subnet A (app)                        + subnet Z (collector)
  | - app-01                              | - mirror-01.ingest: listen:9200
  | - app-02 -- fw -> nat-gw -- internet -|                         ^
  | - sidecar mTLS  <-->  ingress-gw      |                         | (sflow/netflow / pcap)
  +---------------------------------------+-------------------------+

Traffic path notes:
- East-west app traffic should be allowed only on service ports and be mTLS-terminated at the application proxy.
- North-south egress is strictly NATed with egress rules logged at the gateway.
- Traffic mirroring (tap) is enabled on the gateway in a read-only fashion and forwarded to the collector subnet.

RBAC v2: quick principles and recommended roles
- Principle of least privilege: grant access by role, not by IP or ad-hoc groups.
- All evidence-related API calls must go through an audited service account.
- Time-bound temporary elevation using short-lived grants (1h–8h) with justifications preserved in audit logs.

Suggested roles (names and short description):
- evidence_viewer: read-only access to evidence artifacts and SIEM query results. No ability to export raw PCAPs.
- evidence_analyst: can create and run captures, annotate artifacts, request export. Exports require approval if target is external.
- evidence_admin: configure mirror targets, rotate collector credentials, manage retention policies.
- incident_investigator (temp grant): full read access to raw captures for a bounded window; elevation requires approval ticket ID in the grant metadata.

RBAC v2 enforcement checklist:
- [ ] All roles defined in IAM repo with descriptive labels and expiration defaults.
- [ ] Service accounts used for automation are restricted to single-purpose scope.
- [ ] Every access grant emits an audit event with actor, reason, ttl, and ticket/link.
- [ ] Build automated revoke job for temp grants older than TTL + 15m.

Audit log schema (canonical example)
- We expose a compact audit event schema we send to SIEM and to evidence bundles. Events are newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with consistent fields. Example event (presented inline as text):

{
  "ts": "2024-10-22T15:23:11Z",
  "event_id": "evt-0a1b2c3d",
  "actor": "service-account:evidence-collector@redwood-corp",
  "actor_id": "sa-12345",
  "action": "capture.start",
  "resource": "mirror-collector/mirror-01/pcap-20241022-1523",
  "scope": "customer:acme-corp:env:prod",
  "params": {"filter":"dst port 443 and src net 10.0.0.0/16", "capture_mode":"pcap", "max_size_mb":"500"},
  "result": "accepted",
  "outcome": "started",
  "ip": "10.0.10.23",
  "actor_groups": ["eng-private-deployments","sec-incident"],
  "ticket": "INFRA-3421",
  "correlation_id": "corr-abcdef-01",
  "signature": "sha256:...",
  "proto_version": "audit-v2"
}

Notes on schema: params may contain free-form strings but must never contain full secrets or raw private keys. Any PII must be redacted before SIEM export. Use the correlation_id to join network captures with application-level logs.

SIEM export mapping (fields we push)
- timestamp => ts
- host.service => resource
- user.id => actor_id
- event.type => action
- event.outcome => outcome
- net.src_ip, net.dst_ip => ip fields (split)
- file.hash => signature
- meta.ticket => ticket
- labels => actor_groups

Export considerations and transformations:
- Exports to external customer SIEM must be filtered to the customer's scope only (scope field) and must have PII scrubbed.
- Maintain a mapping table for redaction rules per customer.
- Batch events into hourly NDJSON files and sign+hash each bundle before export.

Evidence automation pipeline (recommended flow)
1) Trigger: incident ticket or scheduled capture job (cron) referencing a capture template.
2) Job controller creates a capture job via the mirror API using the automation service account.
3) Capture streams to ephemeral collector disk limited by max_size_mb.
4) On completion, a collector pod computes sha256 for the artifact, extracts a small meta-summary (first/last ts, top talkers), and uploads artifact to evidence-store (object storage) using customer-scoped prefix.
5) Automation posts an audit event (capture.complete) with artifact path, signature, and retention TTL.
6) If export is requested, evidence-export workflow validates redaction rules, then pushes bundles to SIEM endpoint.

Automated retention policy (default):
- Raw PCAPs: 30 days for prod by default; extendable via approved exception.
- Summary metadata and hashes: 365 days.
- Audit events: 395 days (for regulatory needs).

Collector security and deployment notes:
- Run mirror-collector pods in a separate subnet with restrictive NSGs. Collector credentials are rotated weekly and stored in the customer KMS.
- Collector uses mutual TLS to push artifacts to the evidence-store endpoint; client certs are pinned.
- Access to raw collector nodes is disabled; only the automation service account may request downloads.

Firewall / VPC rule patterns (recommended minimal set)
- Allow list: within VPC, allow app<>app on service ports {8000, 8080, 9000} only from service CIDR.
- Gateway egress: NAT gateway outbound to customer-approved IP ranges; log and mirror every egress flow.
- Management plane: SSH/RDP locked to jump hosts in a separate mgmt subnet; log access and require 2FA.
- Mirror traffic: mirror source -> collector only on mirrored-port protocol (tap). No reverse connections from collector to mirrored instances.

Example firewall rules (pseudo):
- fw-001: allow tcp 8000 from 10.0.20.0/24 -> 10.0.30.0/24 (service mesh)
- fw-002: deny all ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to 10.0.0.0/16 except ports 80/443 via ingress-gw
- fw-003: allow tcp 9200 from collector-subnet -> SIEM-ingest-endpoint (TLS only)
- fw-004: allow udp 6343 from gateway -> collector (sFlow)

mTLS hardening checklist (deployable steps)
- [ ] Use short-lived certs for pod-to-pod mTLS (rotation <= 24h if possible).
- [ ] Ensure certs are issued by customer-trusted CA or HSM-backed CA.
- [ ] Enforce mutual authentication at the proxy level; fail closed on cert validation errors.
- [ ] Log mTLS handshake metadata to audit events (subject, issuer, cipher suite, validity).
- [ ] Monitor for certificate anomalies (unusual issuer chain, unexpected subject).

Forensic capture runbook (short)
- Pre-reqs: incident ticket ID, approved temporary role, collector availability check.
- Step 1: Create capture job with filter scoped to suspected IPs and ports; include ticket ID in params.
- Step 2: Start capture for a predetermined window (e.g., 15m) or until max_size.
- Step 3: On complete, compute artifacts: sha256, summary, pcap -> evidence-store/customerX/incidents/INFRA-3421/pcap-yyy.pcap
- Step 4: Post capture.complete event and attach ticket id and investigator.
- Step 5: If export required, run redaction job then deliver to SIEM via secure signed bundle.

Acceptance criteria for release of this pattern to customer blueprint
- Automation can create a capture and produce signed artifact without manual steps.
- RBAC v2 temporary elevation flows included and audited.
- Example SIEM export tested end-to-end with POA&M demonstrating redaction.
- Documentation and runbooks exist in the customer-facing folder and in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).

Open items / TODOs:
- Decide default raw pcap retention per region (legal review pending).
- Add standardized labels for correlation (service.version / deploy_id).
- Build a lightweight UI for evidence download requests that embeds the approval workflow.
- Implement automatic PII detection / redaction step for exports.

Quick references and links:
- Infra ticket for prototype: INFRA-3421
- Confluence draft: conf:private-deployments-evidence-playbook
- PR with automation code: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR-789

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive: creates a baseline that SREs can operationalize in a customer's VPC without revealing internal secrets. Please comment on whether temporary grant TTLs are acceptable and the proposed retention windows.

End of playbook (working draft).
